Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The current bug report indicates a problem with the node() implementation in DOM and JDOM models. Specifically, in DOMNodePointer.java at line 120, the code that matches nodes when using node() only returns true for elements and the document node types:

```
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE :
  return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
```

However, the semantics of node() in XPath indicate that it should match any node type (element, text, comment, processing instruction, document, etc.). The bug report suggests that this should be changed to simply return true for all node types.

This aligns with the failing test snippet case. The test is asserting the following axis with node():

```java
// following:: with a namespace
assertXPathPointer(context, "//location[2]/following::node()[2]", "/vendor[1]/product[1]");
```

The test is checking navigation following nodes. If node() only matches elements and document nodes, it misses other node types, potentially causing the test to fail because it won't find the expected nodes in the axis.

The root cause is therefore the restrictive logic for node() matching in the DOM and JDOM models as implemented in their respective NodePointer classes. They currently do:

- Match only ELEMENT_NODE or DOCUMENT_NODE for node()
- But it should match any kind of node unconditionally for node()

No other recent bug reports directly mention this core issue. This matches the failure symptom exactly, where node() usage in axis navigation is broken.

Hence, the bug is that node() is not implemented correctly in the DOMNodePointer and the equivalent JDOMNodePointer by restricting to element/document node types rather than all node types. This causes failures in XPath expressions making use of node().

Next, it is most useful to locate the exact method in DOMNodePointer and JDOMNodePointer that implements this node() matching and fix the logic.

This concludes the step-by-step diagnosis using the failing test, current bug report, and code snippets found.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
